rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Standing finding, re-checked with fresh per-bullet word counts (both chunks are untouched by the pinned diff, which only edited chunks 2, 4 and 6). Chunk 5 'Design principles' bold-span word counts: 6, 6, 5, 3, 7, 4, 5 across its 7 bullets -- 3 of 7 clearly exceed the ~5-word handle cap (6, 6, 7 words). Chunk 7 'What's special about this stack' bold-span word counts: 3, 5, 4, 4, 4 across its 5 bullets -- none numerically exceeds 5. Correcting the prior instance's evidence, which claimed both chunks 'exceed it on every bullet': on a pure word-count read that overstates chunk 7 and 4 of chunk 5's 7 bullets. The REVISE nonetheless stands on the rule's OTHER, independent test: 'never a whole lead sentence' -- every single bullet in both chunks (12 of 12) bolds its ENTIRE lead sentence, full stop included, then continues in plain prose (e.g. line 122 '**Composition over inheritance.** Skills don't extend or wrap each other.'; line 155 '**Front-loaded read-only analysis.** Five PLAN-phase skills...'). That is the rule's own named violation shape verbatim: 'every bullet on a slide opens with a bolded sentence (the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture) -- flatten to handles or prose.' Handles must be a sub-span pulled from within a longer sentence, not the sentence itself however short. This is a supplementary/lookup page so the per-slide <=1-bold budget is waived by §9's reading-list/lookup-surface carve-out, but that carve-out explicitly preserves the handle-as-sub-span requirement ('bold the label, not the sentence after it'), which both chunks violate on every bullet.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Pull a short label out of each lead and unbold the rest of the sentence (e.g. '**No duplication.** A skill never duplicates another's logic...' or '**Front-loaded analysis.** Five PLAN-phase skills...') in both Design Principles and What's special about this stack.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.

This file is a supplementary reference/progressive-reading page, not an exercise or lecture, so the binary mood contract doesn't bind it the same way; headings here are a mix of topical labels ('Diagrams', 'Skill catalog by phase') and one imperative worksheet heading ('Map your own kit'), consistent with a lookup/reference register rather than a violation of either mood.
